Items.Authors: John J. Piotrowski, Danielle Frostig, Mark Mueller, David Cruz, Matthew Werneken, Julian Garcia, Daniel Fabricant, Ashley Villar, Ana Bonaca, Phillip A. Cargile, Vedant Chandra, Charles Conroy, Benjamin D. Johnson
Items.Title: Optical design of Boombox: a high-throughput optical spectrograph on dual-hemisphere 6.5-meter telescopes
Items.Abstract: Boombox is a moderate-dispersion optical spectrograph currently being built for the 6.5-meter MMT and Magellan Clay telescope. Boombox, in synergy with the LSST, will provide rapid follow-up spectroscopy of LSST targets to classify the diverse array of expected transient astronomical phenomena and their host galaxies. In this paper, we present the optical design of Boombox and provide a detailed tolerance analysis to ensure manufacturability. Boombox achieves its scientific goals with a two-channel spectrograph covering 3550 to 10100 Å at R ~ 1000. The spectrograph uses 36 dedicated optical fibers (1.2" core diameter) from the Via fiber positioning system distributed across a 1-degree field of view. Boombox leverages binary transmission gratings and a high QE deep-depleted CCD261-04 to achieve high throughput. Finally, we discuss the optical design challenges associated with minimizing spectral crosstalk and provide lessons learned for future spectrograph designs.

Items.Authors: John J. Piotrowski, Daniel Fabricant, Daniel Catropa, Ana Bonaca, Charlie Conroy, Vedant Chandra, Phillip A. Cargile, Andrew Cline, Banjamin D. Johnson, Mark Mueller, William Podgorski, Joseph Zajac
Items.Title: Optical design of the Via Instrument: a wide-field radial velocity survey spectrograph on dual-hemisphere 6.5-meter telescopes
Items.Abstract: The Via Project is a 5-year all-sky radial velocity survey and instrument currently being constructed with an expected commission date in 2027. The survey will be conducted simultaneously on the 6.5 m MMT and Magellan Clay telescope. The Via Survey will constrain the dark matter environment of the Milky Way through radial velocity and metallicity measurements of stellar streams and local dwarf galaxies. The survey will also reconstruct the 3D structure and kinematics of cold gas in the local CGM through Na I D absorption tomography. The Via Instrument is composed of the fiber positioning system (FPS) and the bench spectrograph (Viaspec). The FPS distributes ~600 robotically reconfigurable optical fibers across a 1° field of view. Viaspec covers 5050–5950 Å at a resolving power of R = 15,000. The spectrograph uses high-efficiency (>90%) gratings, a 1373 mm EFL collimator, and a six-element 410 mm EFL camera design. We present the expected performance and status of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Marco Xompero, Armando Riccardi, Nicolò Azzaroli, Runa Antonio Briguglio Pellegrino, Giorgio M. Pariani, Pietro Ferraiuolo, Matteo Menessini, Luca Oggioni, Chiara Scandaglia
Items.Title: Optical surface and cavity reconstruction from sub-aperture measurements
Items.Abstract: Large optics have become mandatory with the new generation of large telescope, in which not only the primary mirror is segmented. In this work we are introducing a new approach to estimate the optical surface of a mirror. With using partial surface measurement like in a standard stitching approach, we will populate our surface estimation using a continuously refined reconstructor optimum in a least-square way, converging to a stable solution granting surface continuity. We will estimate in the same time the cavity error and the alignment error for each single measurement of the partial optical surface..The base chosen for the estimation are the Zernike modes by Noll. Optical surfaces will be estimated together with caviry and alignment in a single minimization process.

Items.Authors: Salvador Cuevas, Joel Sánchez-Bermudez, Rebeca Garcia-López, Gerhard Ulbricht, Fernando Angeles, Alejando Farah, Ruben A. Flores-Meza, Yair Misael Maldonado Gómez, Carolina Keiman, Valente Vázquez-Velázquez, Aaron Cruz-Ramirez, Diego Zimarrön-Hernández, Frank Eisenhauer, Tibeau Paumard, Jean-Baptiste Le Bouquin, Laura Kriedberg, P. J. V. Garcia, Sebastian F. Hoenig, Carl Straubmeier, Helmut Feuchtgruber, Guillaume G. Bourdarot, Dieter Lutz, Frank Haussmann, Christian Rau, Luis C. Alvarez-Nuñez
Items.Title: Optical verification of the new Ge grism for GRAVITY+ SUPER HIGH-RES mode
Items.Abstract: In this work, we present the optical tests carried out on the high-resolution Ge grism for GRAVITY+. We describe the dimensional tests of the grism ,including the faces angles and the number of lines/mm, using an optical goniometer.   The figure of the faces was measured using a ZYGO VeriFire Fizeau interferometer. We also estimated the roughness of the grism faces by means of an additional optical system coupled to the ZYGO interferometer. Furthermore, we describe an alternative verification of the number of lines/mm using an electronic microscope.   The transmission in the K band at cryogenic temperatures was crucial for the validity of the grism. We describe the optical setup, which includes a special cryostat, and the obtained results in the laboratory of this transmission value.

Items.Authors: florian cheyssial, Cyril Petit, Laurent Mugnier
Items.Title: Optimal exposure time for satellite imaging? A trade-off between residual tip/tilt and registration accuracy
Items.Abstract: Adaptive-Optics corrected astronomical imaging and satellite imaging from the ground share many commonalities but have also specificities. In particular satellites are non-stationary objects in terms of both shape and flux, encouraging shorter exposure time. Besides, very short exposures freeze the turbulence and enable measuring higher spatial frequencies, but at the cost of a low image SNR, which complicates the post processing. Conversely, too long exposures lead to blurred images where high frequency information is lost.    We propose a method for determining the optimal exposure time regarding the image quality after post-processing. Our model is based on the object type and flux, on the residual aberrations power spectral densities and on the noise level. First, we consider the case where the residual aberrations are only tip/tilt residues and telescope's vibrations. Then, we consider the variations of higher order aberrations (i.e. that the PSFs differ from one image to another).

Items.Authors: Yinzi Xin, Sebastiaan Haffert, Rico Landman
Items.Title: Optimal mode-sorting coronagraphy for exoplanet detection and characterization
Items.Abstract: Conventional coronagraph architectures struggle to reach the theoretical limit of exoplanet detection at close working angles. Spatial mode-sorting is capable of reaching the theoretical limit. We have calculated optimized nulling modes as a function of the size of the star and planet parameters, with the goal of improving coronagraphic performance at ~1 l/D working angles given partially resolved stars and complex telescope apertures. We explore the limits of a coronagraph involving the measurement of a single spatial mode, with potential applications for the infrared arm of the Habitable Worlds Observatory. We present the achievable single-channel 1 l/D planet throughput as a function of the single-channel stellar suppression (for a 0.03 l/D diameter star), and show that the ability to measure a single optimized spatial mode can allow us to reach at least ~80% of the theoretical information limit.

Items.Authors: Makoto Komaki, Yuji Ikeda, Kenta Sakabe, Shin Oya
Items.HTMLTitle: Optimal weighting functions and altitude sampling for accurate estimation of C 2 n profile
Items.Title: Optimal weighting functions and altitude sampling for accurate estimation of C2n profile
Items.Abstract: Atmospheric turbulence profiling is essential for adaptive optics tomography and ground-to-satellite optical communication. However, conventional scintillation profilers are limited by poor altitude resolution and sensitivity to measurement noise because their weighting functions are highly redundant. We propose CAMPUSS (Concentric Aperture Masking PUpil-plane Scintillation Sensor), which uses concentric aperture masks as spatial-frequency filters to generate localized weighting functions and selects reconstruction grids by QR pivoting. Simulations using single-layer, two-layer, and continuous turbulence models show that CAMPUSS improves reconstruction accuracy and altitude resolution compared with MASS and RINGSS. The 16-grid configuration achieved performance comparable to or better than RINGSS under the same number of grids, while the 32-grid configuration provided the highest accuracy and stable reconstruction, demonstrating kilometer-scale altitude sampling for AO tomography.

Items.Authors: Leon Olde Scholtenhuis, Jurre Heeringa, Alkistis Kyriakidou, Nikita A. Soshnin, Kevin Kouwenhoven, David J. Thoen, Jochem Baselmans, Sten Vollebregt, Akira Endo
Items.Title: Optimizing deposition conditions and dielectrics for parallel-plate capacitor KIDs in TIFUUN ifus
Items.Abstract: Probing early-universe star formation with TIFUUN requires an on-chip Integral Field Unit (IFU) containing ~15,000 Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs) on a 4-inch wafer. This necessitates compact KID designs, such as Parallel Plate Capacitor (PPC) KIDs.  However, the sensitivity of these devices is often limited by two-level-system (TLS) noise originating in the intra-plate dielectric, whose dependence on deposition conditions remains poorly understood.  Here we present frequency-noise measurements of NbTiN PPC resonators employing ICP-PECVD a-Si:H dielectrics, and relate these results to the corresponding deposition conditions and film properties. Based on these findings, we propose a PPC KID geometry and dielectric process that meets the requirements of TIFUUN’s IFU.

Items.Authors: Rhonda M. Morgan, Renyu Hu, Mario Damiano, Michael Turmon, Dmitry Savransky, Eric Mamajek, Bertrand Mennesson, Tyler D. Robinson, Armen Tokadjian
Items.Title: Optimizing HWO architectures for distinguishing sub-Neptune size planets as rocky planets, water worlds, or mini-Neptunes
Items.Abstract: Sub-Neptune-sized planets are among the most common in our galaxy, yet it is currently unknown what fraction of sub-Neptune sized planets are rocky planets, water worlds, or gas-dominated mini-Neptunes. In addition to helping understand exoplanet formation and diversity, some larger-than-Earth planets with solid surfaces or oceans could support life. The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) could perform atmospheric characterization to distinguish types of sub-Neptunes. We evaluate exoplanet characterization yields for sub-Neptunes utilizing our framework to perform a significant number of end-to-end yield simulations in a multivariate parameter sweep in the optical wavelengths. By exploring the spectral quality over a broad architecture space, the multivariate parameter sensitivity reveals the intricacies within the trade space and helps to inform high level science performance requirements for the HWO Solar Systems in Context Working Group.

Items.Authors: S. Thoms, M. Timpe, M. Reichert
Items.Title: Optimizing wavefront-deformation sensor placement for active radio-telescope surfaces
Items.Abstract: A general optimization framework is presented for determining efficient placement of surface-deformation sensors on radio-telescope reflectors. Using telescope-specific finite-element load cases, the method identifies sensor configurations that maximize deformation-field reconstructability across relevant operational conditions. The approach enables both performance evaluation for a fixed sensor budget and determination of the minimum number and distribution of sensors required to meet a specified accuracy target, supporting next-generation active-surface radio telescopes.

Items.Authors: Julien Storm, Gert Raskin, Christian Schwab, Jake Pember, Nick Binos, Louis Storm, Bart Vandenbussche
Items.Title: Optomechanical considerations for extreme thermo-mechanical stability: insights from the MARVEL high resolution echelle spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The MARVEL spectrograph is designed to deliver extreme precision radial velocity (EPRV) measurements over time series that extend across months and years. Achieving this performance requires instrument stability at the level of ≤13 nm, equivalent to 1 m/s RV precision. Therefore, MARVEL is housed in vacuum and relies on an optomechanical design that minimizes deformations and mechanical stress while incorporating alignment mechanisms engineered for long-term stability. Here we describe the kinematic mounting approaches, flexure implementations, and overall optomechanical design choices that together will enable MARVEL to maintain extreme thermo mechanical stability and nanometer scale invariance over years of operation.

Items.Authors: Devika K. Divakar, Andrew Pinckney, Joseph Strubhar, Phillip MacQueen
Items.Title: Optomechanical design of an ADC and image rotator for the HJST Coudé spectrograph at McDonald Observatory
Items.Abstract: High-resolution spectroscopy with the Harlan J. Smith 2.7 m Telescope (HJST) benefits from stable image quality and controlled atmospheric refraction. We present the design of a Rotational Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector (RADC) and a Dove-prism based image rotator for the coudé Tull spectrograph. Atmospheric dispersion produces wavelength-dependent shifts that increase with zenith distance; across 350–1000 nm, the displacement reaches ~3.5″ at a 60° zenith angle, reducing throughput away from the guiding wavelength. The RADC employs counter-rotating Amici prisms to provide continuous chromatic correction, while the Dove rotator stabilizes the instrument position angle and mitigates field rotation during long exposures on non-point-like targets. Together, these subsystems support consistent slit illumination and improved spectral fidelity. We summarize the optical and mechanical design approach, integration considerations, and expected gains in throughput and image stability.

Items.Authors: Justin R. Fletcher
Items.Title: Optomech: a GPU-accelerated optomechanical simulation environment for visuomotor control of hybrid optical telescopes
Items.Abstract: Direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets would enable unambiguous detection of the chemical signatures of exoplanetary  life. To form such an image, even for nearby planetary systems, an astronomical instrument must be sensitive to  1e−9 contrast while achieving an angular resolution on the order of 10 milliarcseconds. Fizeau optical interferometric telescopes that employ lightweight primary optical support structures may satisfy these challenging requirements at a feasible cost, but only if they are able to sustain differential motion of ~1 wave of error between the primaries. To address this optomechanical control task, we introduce and evaluate several visuomotor control approaches using a GPU-accelerated optomechanical simulation environment. We establish baseline results indicating successful closed-loop correction of differential motion, and describe several pathways for future development.

Items.Authors: Reuben Neate, Tinus Stander, Roelf Botha
Items.Title: Packaging and deployment of a lightweight, low-cost, water vapour radiometer for site surveying
Items.Abstract: We present the latest developments on PILCHARD, a K-band dual-channel, 24 / 31.4 GHz, planar integrated low-cost water vapour radiometer developed for site surveying. We present selected details of the instrument lab performance, packaging requirements and integration of the instrument into a larger weather station, as well as preliminary qualification data.

Items.Authors: Haisheng Zhao
Items.Title: Particle identification methods and results for the follow-up X-ray telescope onboard Einstein Probe
Items.Abstract: Background removal is an important issue in data reduction for the Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT) onboard the Einstein Probe (EP), particularly for the particle-induced background. The particle-induced background in the FXT comprises background directly caused by particles, as well as instrument events that are also due to particles. A new rejection method, which involves cluster identification, and threshold veto for number of hits in rows and columns, is applied to remove the particle-induced background. The remaining background can be eliminated by the event reconstruction algorithm and event veto in subsequent FXT data reduction. It is shown that their methods can achieve a background rejection eﬀiciency of > 99.8 %. Additionally, there has been a notable decrease in the number of spikes in the light curves of the FXT. Furthermore, we found the instrument background is attributed to a combination of particles and CAMEX electronics.

Items.Authors: Elora Lefebvre, Marcel Carbillet, Olivier Lai, Lyu Abe, François-Xavier Schmider, Nhu Tin Mai, Julien Dejonghe, Jean-Pierre Rivet
Items.Title: Performance assessment of the AOC system on a 1-m telescope: stellar mode characterisation and planetary mode development
Items.Abstract: The AOC (Adaptive Optics at Calern) system aims to bring AO correction to 1-m class telescopes, which typically lack such capabilities, enhancing their high-angular resolution imaging performance. It offers both stellar (8.5″ FoV) and planetary (30.5″/80.5″ FoV) modes, guiding either on point sources or extended objects (such as Jupiter or Saturn). In the latter case, it introduces a filtering of the high-altitude turbulence, similar to ground-layer AO averaging, because high-altitude turbulence will be different around the edges of the planet, distorting the planetary disk, but not necessarily shifting the overall centroid.    This work focuses on the ongoing characterisation and optimisation of the system, from near-infrared to visible wavelengths. We are developing both simulation tools and diagnostic/evaluation tool, and comparing simulations, telemetry, and on-sky data, aiming at refining wavefront control and improving robustness for both stellar and planetary observations.

Items.Authors: Matteo Menessini, Lorenzo Busoni, Simone Esposito, Guido Agapito
Items.Title: Performance comparison of multistage ExAO systems for high contrast imaging
Items.Abstract: The performance of the next generation of instruments for high contrast imaging on ground telescopes relies on the correction provided by an extreme adaptive optics (XAO) system. In this contribution, we study, through end-to-end simulations, the performance of a multi-stage XAO system to enable high contrast at small angular separations. We focus on the wavefront sensing and control aspect of the problem, optimizing the XAO loop upstream the coronograph to maximize contrast in the post-coronographic PSF. Existing AO loop algorithms and strategies are adapted to this new merit function. We consider different telescope apertures and coronograph types, concluding with the simulated performance tailored to the dual-stage system for RISTRETTO, a high-resolution IFU spectrograph proposed for the VLT.

Items.Authors: Malcolm C. Scarrott, Yuk Shan Cheng, Jake Charsley, Richard A. McCracken, Derryck T. Reid, Lisa A. Crause, Daniel L. Holdsworth, William Newman, Willem J. van der Westhuizen, Etienne L. Simon
Items.Title: Performance of the laser frequency comb for the red channel of SALT's high-resolution spectrograph
Items.Abstract: We report on the completion of the integration and initial testing of a bespoke laser frequency comb (LFC) for the red channel (555-890 nm) of the High-Resolution Spectrograph (HRS) on the Southern African Large Telescope (SALT). The comb is driven by a 1 GHz Ti:sapphire laser, a photonic crystal fibre is used for supercontinuum generation, a plano-concave Fabry-Pérot cavity filters the modes to yield the required 20 GHz comb spacing, and a spatial light modulator is employed in the spectral flattening module before comb light is delivered to the spectrograph via a single-mode fibre. A precision radial velocity data reduction pipeline is being developed in Python to support the high-stability mode of the HRS that will make provision for simultaneous wavelength calibration. Future work aims to render the HRS LFC a turn-key system.

Items.Authors: Miguel Andrés Sánchez Carrasco, Stefan Cikota, Marina Centenera-Merino, Javier Flores, Pedro José Amado-González, Jesús Aceituno-Castro, David Pérez-Medialdea, María Isabel Ruiz-López, Francisco J. Pozuelos, Kalaga Madhav, Julius Göhring, Abani Shankar Nayak, Sergio León-Saval, José Luis Ortiz, Martin M. Roth
Items.Title: Photonic E-MARCOT at Calar Alto: architecture and integration of the MARCOT pathfinder spectroscopic mode for on-sky validation of MM–MM photonic lanterns at CAHA
Items.Abstract: The MARCOT Pathfinder is a multi-telescope demonstrator aimed at testing a scalable, fiber-fed spectroscopic architecture based on an array of small optical telescopes at Calar Alto Observatory. Its new spectroscopic mode combines post-focus fiber injection, a spectrograph focal adapter, and telescope control to provide stable coupling into an existing spectrograph interface. This contribution outlines the overall system architecture and the proposed on-sky validation of the spectroscopic mode under representative observing conditions at CAHA.

Items.Authors: Jacob Wirth, James Mason, Alain Carrier
Items.Title: Photonic integrated circuit heterodyne interferometer laser gauges for picometer-class metrology
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) has the ambitious goal of directly imaging and characterizing Exo-earths in search of life in the universe. For HWO to achieve this, the observatory requires a robust wavefront control system (WCS) to maintain wavefront stability to roughly 2 pm over up to 1000 seconds. As part of the larger WCS, HWO will employ a laser metrology truss consisting of many laser metrology gauges to measure the relative pose between the primary mirror segments and the secondary mirror. Lockheed Martin has developed laser metrology gauges with pm-class stability using photonic integrated circuit (PICs) heterodyne interferometers. In this presentation, we report experimental measurements of metrology errors internal to our PIC gauges. We also present an architecture study on placement and orientation of metrology gauges to minimize wavefront error. Additionally, we present a technology readiness level assessment and roadmap for achieving a level 5 for the gauges.

Items.Authors: Felipe Guzman
Items.Title: Picometer optical metrology for future space observatories
Items.Abstract: In this paper, we present the research work of the Laboratory of Space Systems and Optomechanics (LASSO) at the University of Arizona on laser-interferometric metrology technologies aimed at enabling picometer-level dimensional stability sensing and sub-nanoradian angular alignment for large, segmented space telescopes such as the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). Central to this effort is the Optical Truss Interferometer (OTI), a compact and modular Fabry-Perot system that can be distributed across the telescope’s primary and secondary mirrors. Laboratory prototypes have demonstrated sub-picometer displacement sensitivity over representative baselines. Current work focuses on extending this performance to meter-scale cavity lengths while reducing the physical footprint and complexity of the optical heads. Altogether, this research addresses critical technology and metrology developments required for future missions like HWO, contributing toward NASA’s Exoplanet Exploration Program.

Items.Authors: Vincent Revéret, Louis Rodriguez, Albrecht Poglitsch, Eliana Recoba Pawlowski, Laurent Dussopt, Abdelkader Aliane, Valérie Goudon
Items.Title: Polarimetric all silicon bolometric arrays in the submillimeter domain: new results
Items.Abstract: We present the latest developments concerning BBOP detectors, a new generation of “instrument-in-pixel’’ bolometric arrays enabling high-sensitivity submillimeter polarimetry for astrophysical magnetic-field studies. Recent results show substantial sensitivity gains approaching the sub-attoW/√Hz regime at 50 mK, successful validation of the multiplexed readout system, and the first performance measurements at 350 µm, extending earlier 100 µm work. Their orthogonal antennae allow simultaneous Stokes parameter retrieval with fully differential outputs. These advances support upcoming POLARYS observations at APEX and establish BBOP arrays as key components for future balloon-borne and ground-based polarimetric instruments.

Items.Authors: Eduard R. Muslimov, Luca Fossati, Coralie Neiner, Jean-Claude Bouret, Davide Le Mignant, Kjetil Dohlen, Jean-Michel Reess, Adrien Girardot
Items.Title: POLLUX: optical architecture of a high-resolution spectrograph and polarimeter for the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: POLLUX is a European project of a high-resolution spectrograph with polarimetric capabilities for the future Habitable Worlds Observatory. The current top-level optical architecture implies splitting the instrument into five channels, each representing an echelle spectrograph. The far UV channel provides spectropolarimetry in the 100-123 nm range. The medium UV channel operates in a slit/point source spectroscopy or spectropolarimetry modes in the 120-236 nm range. The near UV channel covers the range 234-438 nm with the same set of modes. The target spectral resolving power is 100K. The far UV polarimeter cannot be retracted, but there is an option to bypass it by the telescope re-pointing and increase the transmission by <6 times. In the near and medium UV, the polarimeter can be replaced by a compensator to avoid re-focusing. The far and near-medium parts of the instrument are coupled to the telescope with different mirror relays with optimised coatings and f-numbers.

Items.Authors: Michael A. Reuter, Angelo Fausti, Amanda Ibsen, Tiago Ribeiro, Wouter van Reeven
Items.Title: Practical experience using Apache Kafka as the middleware for the Rubin Observatory control system
Items.Abstract: The Rubin Observatory Control System (Rubin-OCS) is a distributed system with each component in charge of a particular sub-system. Communication between the components is done by means of a software middleware. After the Kafka feasibility study was approved, implementation and testing proceeded for new Kafka based system. Prior to the start of the LSSTCam commissioning campaign, the observatory switched the middleware technology for the Rubin-OCS from DDS to Kafka. The switch to Kafka has allowed the observatory more flexibility to respond to requests for interface upgrades and stability of performance.

Items.Authors: Barbara Pedroni, Eugene B. Seneta, David Buscher
Items.Title: Predictive fast tip-tilt control for the Magdalena Ridge Observatory interferometer
Items.Abstract: The Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer (MROI) will achieve angular resolutions down to 0.6 mas in the optical and near-infrared wavebands. Most of the corrupting influence of the atmosphere on the incoming wavefronts is removed by a Fast Tip-Tilt system at each unit telescope. The potential of predictive control for the FTT system is evaluated through an end-to-end simulation by comparing a conventional integrator with an AR(3)-based LQG controller under realistic turbulence, detector noise, and delay conditions.

Items.Authors: Wenxin Wang, Donghua Zhao, Yuan Liu, Haiwu Pan, Zhixing Ling, Chen Zhang, Weimin Yuan, Shuang-Nan Zhang
Items.Title: Preliminary study of EP-WXT particle-induced background using data by Earth occultation
Items.Abstract: EP, launched on 9 January 2024, is a mission dedicated to time-domain high energy astrophysics. It carries two scientific payloads: the Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT) and the Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT). The EP-WXT consists of 12 identical modules and covers 1/11 of the sky in a single snapshot. Its energy band ranges from 0.5 to 4 keV. Each module contains lobster-eye micropore optics with scientific CMOS (sCMOS) focal-plane detectors. In this work, we present preliminary results of the EP-WXT particle-induced background analysis using data by Earth occultation.

Items.Authors: Manasa Lakshmi Narasimhan, Nicole Melso, David Schiminovich, Rain Naylor
Items.Title: Prototype spectropolarimetry module for lenslet-based integral field spectrographs: design and calibration
Items.Abstract: Integral-field spectropolarimetry enables simultaneous spatial, spectral, and polarization measurements. In tandem with spectral information, polarized emission can be used to map the kinematics of dust expelled from galaxies and to probe the underlying spectrum of scattered light. Our work showcases a prototype design of a compact, off-the-shelf, optical polarization module intended for pairing with lenslet-based integral-field spectrographs, like the Circumgalactic Hα Spectrograph (CHαS). We describe the opto-mechanical layout, data collection scheme, and the strategies used to measure and calibrate possible instrumental polarization. The module enables polarization measurements without requiring major modifications to the optical path and allows for compatibility with existing IFU spectrographs. We will present the design, implementation, and laboratory characterization of this prototype, highlighting its role in enabling future integral field spectropolarimetric measurements.

Items.Authors: Anthony Berdeu, Jean-Baptiste Le Bouquin, Henri Bonnet, Sylvain Oberti, Johann Kolb, Julien Woillez, Guillaume Bourdarot, Thibaut Paumard, Carlos Correia, Denis Defrère, Frank Eisenhauer, Sebastian Hönig, Laura Kreidberg, Florentin Millour, Ferréol Soulez, Christian Straubmeier
Items.Title: Pseudo-synthetic interaction matrix for the GRAVITY+ Adaptive Optics system: modeling and calibration of the ALPAO deformable mirror influence functions and coupling
Items.Abstract: The GRAVITY+ Adaptive Optics systems at the Very Large Telescope are based on 43x43 deformable mirrors  (DM), under-resolved by the different Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensors: 9x9 infrared, 40x40 visible and 30x30  laser guide star. Having a fine model of the DM is crucial to control its shape and ensure that the low order  modes of the control basis do not produce unseen high spatial frequencies. We present how we obtain a two-  dimensional super-resolved model of the DM mean influence function and how we calibrate its coupling matrix.  This allows to produce almost pure low order modes with negligible loss of performances.

Items.Authors: Grace Sweetak, Breann Sitarski, Kevin France, Randall McEntaffer
Items.Title: PyISH: python integral field spectrograph simulation for HWO
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is a large ultraviolet/optical/near-infrared space telescope recommended by the National Academies’ Astro2020 decadal survey. The most recent HWO architectural studies have added an ultraviolet integral field spectrograph (IFS) to the baseline instrument suite. To understand the trade between different instrument parameters, such as spectral and spatial resolution and field of view, we developed PyISH, a UV IFS simulation tool. PyISH models the components of a UV IFS and allows users to provide a broad range of input science cases. The simulation outputs UV IFS-related deliverables, including a three-dimensional data cube based on user-specified input parameters. PyISH provides the user with the ability to explore engineering trades to directly link engineering constraints with science deliverables. PyISH’s components and applications to science, engineering, and HWO will be described in this presentation.

Items.Authors: Jordan D. Wheeler, Anna K. Vaskuri, Jason Austermann, Michael Vissers, Johannes Hubmayr, Shannon Duff, Matthew Koc, Joel Ullom, Simon Doyle, Thomas L. R. Brien, Michael L. Brown
Items.Title: Quasi-lumped element matching of superconducting transmission lines to MKIDs
Items.Abstract: Multichroic, wide-bandwidth millimeter and submillimeter focal planes often require on-chip circuitry to separate astronomical signals spectrally. When using a microwave kinetic inductance detector (MKID), coupling to the mm-wave circuit must be made directly to the MKID inductor. A difficulty is that typical MKID materials have resistances on the order of 1 ohm/square or higher, resulting in a large reactance in the lossy transmission line formed by the MKID inductor. This imaginary part of the impedance is challenging to match to the purely real impedance of a lossless superconducting transmission line. However, complex loads can be matched with lumped elements over a limited bandwidth. As such, we explore coupling schemes employing quasi-lumped-element matching networks, some of which do not require galvanic contact between the transmission line and MKID inductor. These matching networks expand the potential to achieve high detector absorption with fewer constraints on the MKID.

Items.Authors: sini yang, Lin Wen, Qihang Han, Yonghe Chen, Dongge Zhang, Jian Ge, Haijiao Jiang
Items.Title: Radiation-induced performance degradation of optical materials for the Earth 2.0 space mission
Items.Abstract: This study evaluates the radiation tolerance of five optical materials—fused silica, CaF₂, H-LaF10, H-ZF1, and H-ZBaF20—for the Earth 2.0 transit telescopes. Ground-based experiments simulated electron, gamma-ray, and proton irradiation at L2 and measured transmission degradation over 450–960 nm. Results show strong variation in radiation sensitivity: fused silica performed best (<1.5% degradation), while heavy lanthanum glasses were most sensitive, with gamma-ray damage up to 18.3%. Proton irradiation caused the most severe overall degradation. Sequential irradiation produced less damage than cumulative estimates. Findings provide critical data for radiation-resistant optical design of space-based photometric instruments.

Items.Authors: Jimi Green, Shari Breen, Sharmila Goedhart, Andre van Es
Items.Title: Ramping up SKAO science operations for SKA-Low science verification
Items.Abstract: Significant progress is being made with the construction and commissioning of the SKA-Low telescope in Australia at Inyarrimanha Ilgari Bundara, the CSIRO Murchison Radio-astronomy Observatory site. Concurrent with telescope deployment, is the ramp up of telescope operations in order to deliver on the promise of the SKAO to the scientific community. We will discuss the pathway to the SKA-Low telescope surpassing current comparable radio astronomy facilities. With Array Assembly 2, SKAO will conduct its initial Science Verification, providing the community with its first access to SKAO data. The intention of Science Verification is to confirm the end-to-end system functionality of modes and capabilities, in order to build trust within the community, and expose the community to SKA data. We will provide a description of the scaling up of scientific operations with the array assembly deployments, including, scheduling, observing, monitoring and processing of data.

Items.Authors: J. Marco de La Rosa, J. Rosich, M. Luis, O. Tubío, A. Basden, J. Patrón, I. Montilla, R. L. López, M. Puga, R. Simoes, E. González, A. B. Nuñez, H. De Paz, M. Huertas, V. Canto-Caño, E. Joven, S. Fernández, G. Lombardi, J. M. Delgado, M. Reyes García-Talavera, V. J. S. Béjar
Items.Title: Real-time control software for the AO loops of GTCAO
Items.Abstract: GTCAO’s adaptive optics system relies on a real-time AO control loop that senses and reconstructs the wavefront to drive a deformable mirror. To enhance performance and durability, the system includes two additional offloading loops: tip-tilt offload to M2 and global wavefront plus segment tip-tilt offload to M1.  This work presents the architecture of the software that implements these real-time loops and the components interfacing with the telescope’s pointing system and active optics. It also provides an introduction to the main GUI used for the core operation of the instrument. All the software presented here is currently running in production at the GTC as of summer 2026. Key conclusions and lessons learned from the development process are discussed.

Items.Authors: Francesco Di Mille, Gulliermo Blanc, Carlos Contreras, Carlos G. Diaz, Matias Diaz, Marcelo Mora, David Osip, Povilas Palunas, Gabriel Prieto, Lionel Zumaran
Items.Title: Remote observing with the Magellan Telescopes
Items.Abstract: Remote observing at the Magellan Telescopes has evolved into a robust and efficient mode of operation supporting a wide range of programs. Observers prepare their runs in advance through a dedicated online system and connect on observing nights through a system that mirrors the control-room experience at Las Campanas Observatory. With real-time live communication with operators and support astronomers, remote users can monitor the telescope state, carry out calibrations, and execute their observing plans as if they were on site.    The system was designed to preserve the collaborative nature of classical Magellan observing while offering the flexibility required for distributed research teams. This poster will describe the system architecture, operational model, and user experience, along with lessons learned from its adoption at Magellan.

Items.Authors: Haoyang Zhang, Yingfu Wang, Jiahao Zhou, Wengfei Liu, Mengmeng Qian, Xianke Song, Kai Yun, Hongzhuan Hu, Jiangping Wang, Jiaru Chu, Ping Zhang, Zhigang Liu, Zengxiang Zhou
Items.Title: Research on photogrammetric reference based on high-density miniature fiber positioners
Items.Abstract: The LAMOST closed-loop detection system employs a 21mm diameter fiducial fibers. To accommodate the upcoming 10.4mm aperture grouped fiber solution, it's crucial to provide a detection reference for tens of thousands of grouped fiber positioner. This project focuses on researching a high-precision measurement benchmark scheme and designing a reference fiber unit adapted to the 10.4mm aperture focal plane, meeting the current system's demand for high-precision closed-loop detection. The challenge lies in further optimizing and reducing the size of the existing reference fiber unit, which is already quite compact, without affecting its fundamental functions and ensuring the uniformity and stability of the emitted light spot. This design scheme will contribute to more accurate fiber position determination by photogrammetry, improve the stability of the detection system, and ensure the overall reliable operation of the telescope.

Items.Authors: Christoph Baranec, Reed Riddle, James Ou, Suzanne Zhang, Guillaume Huber, Zachary Werber, Luke Mckay, Rachel Rampy, Michael Liu, Carl Ziegler, Mark Chun, Keith Powell, Marcos A. van Dam
Items.Title: Robo-AO-2: entering the era of automated science operations, hybrid wavefront sensing, and adaptive secondary integration
Items.Abstract: We present the first science results and new technical milestones from the Robo-AO-2 facility at the University of Hawaii 2.2-m telescope. Following successful commissioning, the system began science operations in 2025. We are starting a large-scale survey of young stars in the Scorpius-Centaurus association to detect sub-stellar companions, vetting the Habitable Worlds Observatory Target Stars and Systems list, and discovering stellar blends for TESS exoplanet host candidates. We report on the commissioning of the natural guide star wavefront sensor, supporting science and future hybrid laser-stellar sensing demonstrations. Finally, we detail the automation of the telescope facility, Robo88, via updated telescope control systems and absolute encoders, and the integration of Robo-AO-2 with the telescope's new adaptive secondary mirror.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Attoli, Franco Buffa, Francesco Gaudiomonte, Sergio Poppi, Giampaolo Serra, Alessandro Cabras, Gian Paolo Vargiu, Antonietta Fara, Pasqualino Marongiu, Mauro Pili, Gian Luigi Deiana, Giannina Sanna
Items.Title: Sardinia Radio Telescope Metrology System: early commissioning insights
Items.Abstract: Two years after the completion of its high frequency enhancement, the Sardinia Radio Telescope has returned to scientific operations with renewed capabilities, enabling the antenna system to operate up to 116 GHz.  However, observing at the maximum frequency for which the SRT was designed, requires a tighter control of both antenna pointing and main reflector surface accuracy, considering the contribution of environmental loads on its structural behaviour.  The Sardinia Radio Telescope Metrology System (SMS), designed to support the SRT high frequency observations, is fully installed and ready for commissioning tests which are currently under way.  In this regard, the paper summarises the progress achieved over the last two years, describing the activities carried out to characterise tools and instrumentation devoted to metrology applications and presenting the preliminary results.

Items.Authors: Hao Qiu, Boris Sorokin, Danny Price, Ethan Davidson, Federico Di Vruno, Andre Van Es
Items.Title: Satellite constellation simulations for SKAO science operations
Items.Abstract: With the recent rapid development of satellite constellations, we face an increasingly challenging radio spectrum environment for observations. From both known communication frequencies regulated by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and incidental electromagnetic radiation and leakage.   Although satellite ephemerides are generally known, the growing complexity of constellation operations and telescope arrays spread across large areas such as the SKA introduces a multiplexed problem for maintaining a clean spectral environment during observations.  In this paper, we present a comprehensive simulation framework designed to dynamically model satellite emission patterns for radio interferometers. We then present application examples to quantify the impact of satellite constellations on large interferometric arrays and assist with observation planning and scheduling in an increasingly crowded radio spectrum.

Items.Authors: Goeun Kim, Jongguk Choe, Youngchun Youk, Jeeyeon Yoon, Eung Shik Lee, Haeng Pal Heo
Items.Title: Sensitivity and tolerance analysis of a drag-reduced compact Korsch telescope for very low-altitude satellite missions
Items.Abstract: Space telescopes operating in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) are directly affected by atmospheric drag, which significantly impacts their orbital lifetime. This study designed a drag-reduced Korsch telescope considering drag reduction by minimizing the frontal area exposed to the orbital direction. This results in closer distance between the primary and secondary mirrors, which increases sensitivity to alignment errors. This paper presents systematic sensitivity and tolerance analyses comparing the conventional and drag-reduced Korsch designs, examining the feasibility of drag-reduced telescope design for low-altitude missions.

Items.Authors: Freek Roelofs, Christiaan Brinkerink, Albert Catalan Artigas, Heino Falcke, Jaima Fernández, Christian M. Fromm, Felix Glaser, Marc Klein Wolt, Yuri Kovalev, Volodymyr Kudriashov, María Manzano, Rasmus Maråk, Manuel Martin-Neira, Jacobo Pastor Fernández-Posse López, Montserrat Puertolas Turell, Alberto Rodríguez Pérez-Silva, René Rüddenklau, Efthalia Traianou, Roger Vilaseca Miro
Items.Title: SHARPEx: the first space-to-space VLBI experiment
Items.Abstract: Space is the next frontier for high resolution imaging with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI). The limited size of the Earth and atmospheric absorption and turbulence at high frequencies prevent order-of-magnitude resolution improvements from current black hole imaging with the Event Horizon Telescope. A 2 or 3-element submm space-based array like SHARP would image the thin black hole photon ring and measure the black hole spin and spacetime. We present the SHARP Experiment (SHARPEx) mission concept. SHARPEx will demonstrate key enabling technologies for space-to-space VLBI, including clock synchronization between two satellites, on-board correlation, and sub-wavelength orbit determination. SHARPEx will consist of two CubeSat or SmallSat platforms carrying small (~1 m) antennas, observing at cm wavelengths. Depending on the intersatellite link properties (range and bandwidth), a follow-up of SHARPEx may produce images of bright AGN with unprecedented resolution and fidelity.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Lorenzetto, Davide Ricci, Fulvio Laudisio, Daniele Vassallo, Andrea Baruffolo, Domenico Barbato, Maria Bergomi, Elena Carolo, Paolo Cerpelloni, Simone Di Filippo, Valentina D'Orazi, Tania Sofia Gomes Machado, Lorenzo Merli, Davide Greggio, Luca Marafatto, Dino Mesa, Jacopo Farinato
Items.Title: SHINS-OBS : diving in SHARK-NIR's new UI for deep remote access and control
Items.Abstract: SHARK-NIR instrument (System for coronagraphy with high-order AO in Z and H band) is a high-contrast coronagraph imager mounted at the LBT. The instrument's early science verification phase highlighted the necessity for a user-friendly and remotely accessible interface. This was driven by the complex operations required to fully exploit the AO capabilities and successfully complete an observation run. The new web based user interface is presented in all its new features, highlighting the new custom OB-Editor able to prepare all the detailed observing blocks starting from the essential information provided by science case, the immediate control of adaptive optics device and the new direct access to diagnostic data from technical and scientific cameras.  New features of the instrument such as the automatic rotation of the Non Common Path Aberrations following the field derotation are also presented

Items.Authors: Marc-Antoine Martinod, Vincent Foriel, Nick Cvetojevic, Frantz Martinache, Jeronimo Calderon-Gomez, Roxanne Ligi, David Mary
Items.Title: Silencing the stellar glare with kernel-nulling and active phase control on photonic chips
Items.Abstract: Characterizing exoplanets and finding biosignatures are among the hottest topics in astronomy. This quest is challenged by the brightness contrast between the faint planet and the overwhelming glare of the host star, their small angular separation, and observing conditions degraded by optical aberrations. Nulling interferometry is a promising technique to achieve this goal by fulfilling requirements for both high contrast and high angular resolution. Photonic-Integrated Circuits (PICs) provide compactness, design versatility, and scalability needed for nulling. With the PHOTONICS project, we aim to create novel coherent combination architectures, based on a multimode interferometer (MMI) coupler and on-chip active phase control with no moving parts. We will present the first lab tests of a 4-beam kernel-nuller made out of a single MMI coupler with active phase control: ABCD fringe-tracking and the characterization of the contrast detection limits of a four-beam kernel-nuller.

Items.Authors: Corey Spohn, Christopher C. Stark
Items.Title: Simulating images for a complete HWO survey with coronagraphoto
Items.Abstract: Evaluating coronagraph designs for the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) requires image-level simulations spanning a full multi-year mission, yet yield calculators produce only summary statistics, not images. We link a new image-simulation tool, coronagraphoto, to existing HWO mission simulators so that one consistent coronagraph model both schedules a survey and renders its images. We release a public dataset of roughly 6000 rendered frames: 1972 across two independently scheduled multi-year surveys in two bands, and 4032 in a high-fidelity, time- and wavelength-resolved demonstration of a single system. We further show that orbital motion within a deep integration measurably reduces a recovered planet's signal-to-noise, motivating orbit-aware stacking. The dataset is publicly available for developing post-processing algorithms and enabling trade studies between HWO coronagraph designs.

Items.Authors: Donghua Zhao, Lei Wang, Chen Zhang, Wenxin Wang, Zhenqing Jia, Zhixing Ling, Weimin Yuan, Junsheng Cheng, Ping Zhou, Shuangnan Zhang
Items.Title: Simulations and experiments of the electron diverter for the wide-field x-ray telescope onboard the Einstein Probe mission
Items.Abstract: The Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT), the lobster-eye micro-pore optics (MPO) focusing telescope onboard the  Einstein Probe (EP) mission, consists of 12 identical modules. Each WXT module is equipped with a permanent-  magnet diverter to reduce the background induced by low-energy electrons (1–1000 keV). In this paper, we present  the performance of the diverter by simulations and experiments. Based on the experimental and simulation results, the  deflection efficiency of the diverter exceeds 97% for on-axis electrons in the energy range of 100–1200 keV, and the  efficiency is greater than 98% at 1000 keV for electrons with incident angles of Θin ≤ 10◦. Further simulations of a  WXT module show that the background caused by electrons below 1000 keV can be reduced by approximately 90%  with the diverter.

Items.Authors: Radhika Dharmadhikari, Aurélie Magniez, Charlotte Z. Bond, Padmakar Parihar, Kieran O'Brien, Tim Morris
Items.Title: Simulations on petal mode sensing for the ELT using the OTF-based phasing scheme
Items.Abstract: The large spiders in the ELT lead to phase discontinuities of the wavefront, which appear as a piston difference between two sectors of the primary mirror. The adaptive optics system is insensitive to large values of these petal modes and hence a special petalometer device is required, that can measure these petal modes.  We have explored the use of Optical Transfer Function (OTF) based phasing scheme for fast petal mode sensing of the ELT. The performance of this technique under varying external practical conditions for seeing limited as well as AO corrected mode are studied through realistic Python simulations.

Items.Authors: Lukas Weissinger, Simon Hubmer, Bernadett Stadler, Ronny Ramlau
Items.Title: Singular value-based atmospheric tomography with Fourier domain regularization (SAFR)
Items.Abstract: Atmospheric tomography, the problem of reconstructing atmospheric turbulence profiles from wavefront sensor measurements, is an integral part of many adaptive optics systems. To solve this problem, a singular-value decomposition (SVD) based approach has been proposed before. Here, we focus on the numerical implementation of the SVD-based Atmospheric Tomography with Fourier Domain Regularization Algorithm (SAFR) and its performance for MCAO systems. The key features of the SAFR algorithm are the utilization of the FFT and the pre-computation of computationally demanding parts. Together, this yields a fast algorithm with less memory requirements than commonly used Matrix Vector Multiplication (MVM) approaches. We evaluate the performance of SAFR regarding reconstruction quality and computational expense in numerical experiments using the simulation environment COMPASS, in which we use an MCAO setup resembling the physical parameters of the MORFEO instrument of the ELT.

Items.Authors: Emanuele Perinati, Michael J. Freyberg, Michael C. Yeung, Konrad Dennerl, Christian Pommranz, Susanne Friedrich, Ritika Singh, Bastian Hess, Sebastian Diebold, Chris Tenzer, Andrea Santangelo
Items.Title: Soft proton induced background in SRG/eROSITA: a follow-up study
Items.Abstract: The X-ray telescope eROSITA aboard the SRG spacecraft provided measurements of instrumental background at L2, that can be used to acquire knowledge about the experienced radiation environment. In this paper, we aim to make the previously published picture on soft protons more complete and present some results from the analysis of eRASS5 background data. We also compare background data taken in fully open position of the filter-wheel (i.e. without external filter) during a PV-phase Comet observation with that in closed position, so as to quantify the effect of the external filter on background.

Items.Authors: Zhiyuan Ma, Grant Wilson, Itziar Aretxaga, Daniela Espitia-Mosquera, Joseph Golec, Michael McCrackan, Alfredo Montaña, Kamal Souccar
Items.Title: Software framework for TolTEC operation and data automation
Items.Abstract: The TolTEC Camera, mounted on the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT), is a continuum imaging polarimeter  that simultaneously observes at 1.1, 1.4, and 2.0 mm wavelengths. TolTECA v3 is the third major release of the  TolTEC data handling software stack that facilitates TolTEC operation and TolTEC data automation. In this  version, we rewrite the implementation of the data model using a schema-driven design focusing on structured  metadata, and the tolteca_db submodule is now a separate dedicated package built on top of the data models,  providing layered API endpoints for interacting with the data acquisition system, initializing data ingestion  tasks, orchestration of data reduction pipelines, and working as the visualization tooling backend, both during  observation and during post-observation analysis sessions. With TolTECA v3, TolTEC operation is fully automated  throughout the data product lifecycle, from raw data ingestion to data product management.

Items.Authors: Fabrizio Vitali, Matteo Aliverti, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Mirko Colapietro, Federico Battaini, Simone Di Filippo, Sergio D'Orsi, Eugenio Martinetti, Antonio Miccichè, Gaetano Nicotra, Francesco D'Alessio, Davide Ricci, Simone Doniselli, Silvio Di Rosa, Matteo Genoni, Matteo Munari, Salvatore Scuderi, Marco Landoni, Paolo D'Avanzo, Pietro Schipani, Sergio Campana, Armin Silber, Bao Le Van, Ivo Saviane, Derek ives, Mstteo Accardo, Riccardo Claudi, Giulio Capasso, José A. Araiza-Durán, Iair Arcavi, Andrea Baruffolo, Sagi Ben-Ami, Alex Bichkovsky, Anna Brucalassi, Enrico Cappellaro, Rosario Cosentino, Massimo Della Valle, Avishay Gal-Yam, Ofir Hershko, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Luigi Lessio, Laurent Marty, Seppo Mattila, Leander Mehrgan, Giuliano Pignata, Michael Rappaport, Marco Riva, Adam Rubin, Bernardo Salasnich, Ricardo Zanmar Sanchez, Salvatore Savarese, Andrea Scaudo, Stephen Smartt, Maximilian Stritzinger, David Young
Items.Title: SOXS at the NTT: installation and commissioning of the NIR arm
Items.Abstract: SOXS (Son Of X-Shooter) is a single object spectrograph, built by an international consortium for the 3.58-m ESO New Technology Telescope at the La Silla Observatory. It offers a simultaneous spectral coverage over 350-2000 nm, with two separate spectrographs. SOXS is currently mounted at the Nasmyth focus of NTT and, at the time of writing, is completing the technical and scientific commissioning. In this paper we describe the status and the performances of the Near InfraRed arm, as derived from the commissioning in Chile.

Items.Authors: Salvatore Savarese, Marco Landoni, David Young, Davide Ricci, Stephen Smartt, Paolo D'Avanzo, Sergio Campana, Pietro Schipani, Matteo Aliverti, José A. Araiza-Durán, Iair Arcavi, Andrea Baruffolo, Federico Battaini, Sagi Ben-Ami, Alex Bichkovsky, Anna Brucalassi, Giulio Capasso, Enrico Cappellaro, Riccardo Claudi, Mirko Colapietro, Rosario Cosentino, Francesco D'Alessio, Sergio D'Orsi, Massimo Della Valle, Simone Di Filippo, Avishay Gal-Yam, Matteo Genoni, Ofir Hershko, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Luigi Lessio, Laurent Marty, Seppo Mattila, Matteo Munari, Giuliano Pignata, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Michael Rappaport, Marco Riva, Adam Rubin, Bernardo Salasnich, Maximilian Stritzinger, Fabrizio Vitali, Ricardo Zanmar Sánchez, Salvatore Scuderi
Items.Title: SOXS quality control system for operations at the NTT
Items.Abstract: The SOXS spectrograph at the ESO NTT has completed its AIV and Commissioning phases, and a dedicated Quality Control (QC) system is required to monitor performance during routine operations. The SOXS QC framework is organised in two complementary layers. The first relies on ESO Datalab and Grafana to monitor critical telemetry parameters, providing real-time dashboards and a redundant email-based alarm system for the observatory staff and the SOXS Consortium support team whenever predefined thresholds are exceeded. The second focuses on instrument performance by collecting quality metrics produced by the SOXS pipeline from daily calibrations and engineering data. These metrics are consolidated into a dedicated monitoring database and presented as long-term trends, allowing the operations team and the community to verify instrument stability against commissioning baselines and identify gradual performance degradations for predictive maintenance.
